title: Which multiplication is larger without working it out?
description: Two pairs of multiplications from the book are compared without multiplying them out. Each number is written as a middle number plus or minus a small step, so that a square is taken away from a square.
teaching_notes: One idea: write both numbers as a middle number plus or minus a step, so each multiplication becomes a square take away a square, and the smaller step takes away less. Watch for students who just multiply out and miss the pattern.

source: Figure it Out (identities and patterns, question 9)
video_script.why: The child can multiply out two brackets, but has not yet used the pattern of a sum times a take away to compare two multiplications.
video_script.substitution: Write each pair of numbers as a middle number plus and minus a step, and use the pattern from the book for a sum times a take away.
video_script.anchor: the two pairs of multiplications of the book's question, side by side
video_script.payoff_line: In the first pair, sixteen times twenty four is larger.

final_answer.spoken: in the first pair, sixteen times twenty four is larger, and in the second pair, twenty six times seventy four is larger

video_script.design: One idea: a sum times a take away is a square take away a square, so the smaller step takes away less. The two pairs stay on the board through the idea part. The verdict for each pair is left until the answer.

<bookmark mark='first'/>Look at fourteen times twenty six.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Then look at sixteen times twenty four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which is larger, without working either one out?

beats.on_screen: Given: (i) 14 x 26 or 16 x 24 (ii) 25 x 75 or 26 x 74
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two pairs of multiplications from your book.

beats.on_screen: To find: the bigger multiplication in each pair, without multiplying out

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which is larger in each pair, without multiplying out.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, the first pair. Fourteen times twenty six is twenty minus six, times twenty plus six.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Sixteen times twenty four is twenty minus four, times twenty plus four.

marks.rule: the pattern is written: a take away times a sum gives the first squared minus the second squared
marks.first: 400 - 36 is written for the first multiplication
marks.second: 400 - 16 is written for the second multiplication

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, use the pattern from your book. A sum times a take away is the first squared, minus the second squared.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first multiplication is twenty squared minus six squared, which is four hundred minus thirty six.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second is twenty squared minus four squared, which is four hundred minus sixteen.

marks.mid: the middle number 50 is written above the second pair

narration: <bookmark mark='mid'/>Step three, the second pair. The middle number is fifty.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Twenty five times seventy five is fifty squared minus twenty five squared.
<bookmark mark='first2'/>That is two thousand five hundred minus six hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Twenty six times seventy four is fifty squared minus twenty four squared.
<bookmark mark='second2'/>That is two thousand five hundred minus five hundred seventy six.

beats.on_screen: Same start, different take away: 16 is less than 36, and 576 is less than 625

marks.one: 16 is marked as less than 36 under the first pair
marks.two: 576 is marked as less than 625 under the second pair
marks.rule: an arrow shows that the smaller number taken away leaves more

beats.colours: the smaller take away in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step four, compare. In each pair, we start from the same number.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Sixteen is less than thirty six. Five hundred seventy six is less than six hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Taking away the smaller number leaves more.

beats.on_screen: Check by multiplying: 14 x 26 = 364 and 16 x 24 = 384; 25 x 75 = 1875 and 26 x 74 = 1924
narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step five, put the answer back in the question, by multiplying out. Fourteen times twenty six is three hundred sixty four.
<bookmark mark='one2'/>Sixteen times twenty four is three hundred eighty four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Twenty five times seventy five is one thousand eight hundred seventy five.
<bookmark mark='two2'/>Twenty six times seventy four is one thousand nine hundred twenty four.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (i) 16 x 24 is larger (ii) 26 x 74 is larger

marks.ans: (i) 16 x 24 is larger is written and boxed
marks.two: (ii) 26 x 74 is larger is written and boxed
